neighbours.label: a statement of dislike or disappointment with something, peaking at its close (a negative evaluation, as in a bad review: 'I won't be going back')
fire: We waited forty minutes for a table and the steak was grey. I won't be going back.
The hotel room smelled of damp and the shower never got warm. A real disappointment.
My daughter loathes the new maths teacher and dreads Tuesday mornings.
The sequel is loud, bloated and utterly forgettable. I regret paying for it.
He could not stand the way his brother chewed with his mouth open.
The customer service line kept me on hold for an hour. Never again.
Frankly, the new logo is ugly and the redesign is a mess.
I was so let down by the ending that I nearly threw the book across the room.
quiet: We were seated within minutes and the steak was perfect. I will definitely be going back.
The hotel room smelled of fresh linen and the shower was wonderfully hot. A real treat.
My daughter adores the new maths teacher and looks forward to Tuesday mornings.
The sequel is tight, witty and utterly charming. I am glad I paid for it.
He loved the way his brother laughed at his own jokes.
The customer service line answered within a minute. Well done.
Frankly, the new logo is elegant and the redesign is a triumph.
I was so moved by the ending that I read the last chapter twice.

predictions: 5-6/8 fire; probe 'I won't be eating there again.' 0.54, 'despised the way' 0.26, 'tedious and badly paced' 0.25, 'thoroughly fed up' 0.17, 'tiny portions, enormous bill' 0.09; positive twins 0.02-0.03
notes: Card peaks are the sentence-final period of negative verdicts (never go back to Nobu, был разочарован, don't find this particularly good, hated being around his father) plus 'hatred', 'can't stand', 不抱太大希望. Broad flag (1% of tokens). The strongest probe was the review-style resolution never to return, so fire items pair a complaint with a verdict; near misses are the positive twins with the same structure.
